design.scaling: h -> h * target / ||h|| (direction preserved, magnitude set)
design.read_out: raw pre-revin head output; last patch's median channel
design.spectrum: ||P_f y||^2/128 on SPEC_GRID (0.5..9.0 step 0.05, cycles per 32 samples); unit-power tone reads 1 at its own band
design.revin_note: for these unit-power tones the last-patch running stats are exactly mu=0, sigma=1, so the renormalised series equals the raw head output (checked per row via raw_median_vs_ser_max_abs)

reading.B_control: h(4) at unit norm (a 1/46 shrink): r 0.0003, peak 1.25; this is the amplitude-collapse regime (the head is scale-sensitive, not invariant), outside the radii the spike hypothesis concerns
reading.D_smooth: h(5): peak stays 5.35 at every alpha; r/alpha^2 = 0.10796 +- 0.30% over the required alphas.  h(4): peak stays 4.00; r/alpha^2 = 1.30606 +- 1.48%
reading.spike_not_colocated_with_failure: at phi=0 the flank bands have unremarkable norms yet still degrade: 5.1 (||h||=47.9) r=0.662, 5.9 (||h||=47.4) r=0.603; and at phi=1.94 the b=6 input has no big spike (69.9 vs 49.7 for its 5.9 flank, 1.41x) yet still collapses, r=0.0016.  Degradation does not track the norm.
reading.verdict: DIRECTIONAL: the b=5/b=6 head failure is carried by the direction of the block-20 head input.  Removing the norm spike (A) does not recover the tone and imposing it on a working input (C) does not cause a failure, so the spike magnitude is neither necessary nor sufficient; the radial sweep (D) shows only smooth alpha^2 amplitude scaling with no branch flip.
